questions.answerReference:
a. Horizontal motion lasts for only half the flight.
*b. The time rising to maximum height is half of the symmetric total flight time.
c. Gravity acts only during the downward half of the flight.
d. Dividing by 2 converts seconds to meters per second.

questions.prompt: Use your own real or simulated trial that lands at its launch height. State the data source, horizontal distance in meters, and total flight time in seconds. Show four labeled calculation lines: vx = distance/time; vy = 9.8 x time/2; v0 = sqrt(vx^2 + vy^2); and angle = tan^-1(vy/vx) in degree mode. Include substitutions and units. Keep speed and angle on separate lines and use your own values consistently.

questions.prompt: Defend your own trial's calculated launch speed in m/s and mph and explain how the perpendicular velocity components combine. Then analyze two realistic measurement errors. For each, specify whether the measured quantity was too high or too low and explain the effect on the relevant component(s) and calculated result. If you choose timing error, consider both vx = distance/time and vy = 9.8 x time/2; if their effects compete, explain that rather than assuming the total speed must change in one direction. Concise labeled paragraphs or bullet points are welcome.
